evals.name: remote-board
evals.prompt: Set up meerkat for Claude on this repo. The board is at http://board.internal:9527.
evals.expected_output: A detection report that classifies the board as remote, asks before configuring, and runs the installer with --target claude --no-automation (never starting a local taskd). A --dry-run writes nothing.
assertions: The detection report names the requested board URL (or the reachable non-loopback stand-in used for an unresolvable hostname) and classifies it as remote (not loopback).
The plan asks the user to confirm the remote address before writing anything.
The chosen install invocation does not include the server target and does not enable the supervisor.
No file under the temporary HOME is created by the detection or dry-run step.

evals.name: standard-team
evals.prompt: Install meerkat here and build the standard team.
evals.expected_output: Board, loop and setup skills installed for Claude with the server; the standard team installed under the loop skill's roles/ directory, with Claude and Codex native agent definitions. A second run reports every action as unchanged.
assertions: The install uses --target claude and includes the server (or explains why it skipped it).
<home>/.claude/skills/setup-meerkat/SKILL.md exists after installation.
The roles root is <home>/.claude/skills/meerkat-loop/roles with manifest.json, a decision policy, and four roles.
.claude/agents/jobs.md and .codex/agents/reviewer.toml exist.
A second identical run leaves the role files and native agent definitions unchanged (content-hash identical), and the role installer reports every action as unchanged.

evals.name: project-scoped-reviewer
evals.prompt: Use a project-scoped team with a reviewer named Grace.
evals.expected_output: The team is installed under <project>/.meerkat/roles, the global roles skill directory is untouched, the manifest's reviewer agent is Grace, and the effective roles root is the project's.
assertions: <project>/.meerkat/roles/manifest.json exists.
The global <home>/.claude/skills/meerkat-loop/roles is not created or modified.
The reviewer role's agent in the manifest is Grace.
Detection after the install reports the project roles root as the effective root.

evals.name: existing-tracker
evals.prompt: I already have docs/agents/issue-tracker.md for GitHub. Set up the Matt integration.
evals.expected_output: Detection finds the existing unrelated tracker and asks before overwriting; nothing is overwritten without consent. The Matt skill is not invoked through the Skill tool, and the skill does not claim it ran.
assertions: The agent reports that an existing tracker was found and that it is unrelated to taskpanel.
No write to docs/agents/issue-tracker.md happens before the user's confirmation.
The response offers the /setup-matt-pocock-skills command or the manual-read route rather than claiming the skill ran.
A tracker that mentions taskctl or taskpanel is reported as already integrated and skipped.

evals.name: decision-ladder
evals.prompt: A subagent asks an operational question, an epic-split question, and an E2 acceptance question. Show how the loop handles each.
evals.expected_output: The operational and epic-split questions are answered by the project session (a note plus reattach/requeue, no awaiting); the E2 question is escalated to awaiting with options and a recommendation. The subagent writes no decision comment and the loop never uses --as-human for its own answer.
assertions: Each subagent question is recorded as an agent question comment on an in_progress card.
The operational question is answered with a note and a reattach or move to todo, not a decision kind and not awaiting.
The epic split is presented as the project session's decision; only a scope expansion is said to be E1 for the human.
The E2 question becomes issue move ... awaiting --awaiting-reason E2 --question with options and a recommendation.
No example has the subagent writing decision, confirm or change.

evals.name: identity
evals.prompt: Show who is recorded as creator, assignee and report author for a Jobs card, and what a human decision records.
evals.expected_output: Jobs is the board agent name (with --assignee-kind agent / --reporter-kind agent where applicable); a human decision is recorded with --as-human and signs the fixed TASKCTL_HUMAN name, never the role name.
assertions: The example creator, assignee and report author are the role's board agent name (Jobs).
Assignee and reporter writes carry --assignee-kind agent / --reporter-kind agent.
The human decision example uses --as-human and does not use a role name as the human identity.

evals.name: setup-interview
evals.prompt: Set up Meerkat TaskPanel for Claude on this repo. The board is remote at http://board.internal:9527, I want a project-scoped team, and I am not sure the standard team fits. Do not install or write anything - show me the setup interview you would run first.
evals.expected_output: Detection first, used as facts; one numbered frontier round with recommended answers worded so 'yes' accepts them; the standard-team fit is challenged with a counterexample card shape; no install, write or daemon before the frontier closes.
assertions: The response runs detection (or names the facts it would detect) before asking, and never asks for a fact detection can establish.
The open decisions are one numbered round (Q1..Qn), each with a recommended answer worded so 'yes' accepts it.
The team question is adversarial: it asks for a counterexample card or a card shape that would fall between roles.
No install, file write or daemon start happens before the frontier is empty and the answers are confirmed.
--yes is described as accepting only recommended non-destructive answers.

evals.name: custom-team-co-design
evals.prompt: Design a custom team for a product with heavy docs and mobile work. We have Jobs/Linus/Turing today, but docs changes and release notes keep falling through, and nobody is clearly testing the mobile app. Do not install anything; show the team design and the questions you would settle first.
evals.expected_output: A card-shape ownership matrix with exactly one accountable role per shape; at least one unowned or double-owned shape named as a finding; a counterexample card; an independent reviewer; one numbered round; no install before the frontier closes.
assertions: The design lists card shapes and gives each exactly one accountable role.
At least one shape (docs/release notes or mobile testing) is named as unowned or double-owned, as a finding.
It asks for a concrete counterexample card the proposed split would get wrong.
The reviewer remains independent and the ladder (subagent -> main session -> human) is unchanged.
The questions are one numbered round with recommendations, and nothing is installed.

evals.name: decision-round
evals.prompt: A Jobs card has four open decisions: the design register, the mobile breakpoint, a terminology conflict, and whether to expand scope to cover a second persona. Show the decision round Jobs sends and how the loop handles each answer.
evals.expected_output: One question comment carrying Q1..Q4 with recommendations; the operational items answered by the project session in one note with one move; E3 (register) and E1 (scope expansion) escalated in one awaiting string; the subagent writes no decision kind and never enters awaiting; only a human comment resumes.
assertions: The four items are one question comment (Q1..Q4), each with a recommendation, not four separate comments.
The design register (E3) and the scope expansion (E1) are escalated to the human, not decided by the subagent or the project session.
The terminology conflict and the breakpoint are answered by the project session in one note, then the card moves once.
The subagent keeps the card in_progress, writes no decision/confirm/change, and does not enter awaiting.
Only a human comment resumes awaiting; an incomplete answer is not consent.
